reason: The text establishes and reinforces a clear hierarchical structure throughout. God commands Moses, who selects twelve representatives (one from each tribe) described explicitly as 'heads of the children of Israel' (רָאשֵׁי בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל). These representatives are elevated above the general population. The narrative reinforces this hierarchy: Caleb demonstrates leadership authority by silencing the people (וַיַּהַס כָּלֵב אֶת־ הָעָם), and those who challenge the authority of Moses and Aaron are depicted as sinful and punished by God. The text concludes by affirming that those loyal within the hierarchical structure (Joshua and Caleb) are rewarded with inheritance, while those who questioned authority die in the wilderness. The consistent pattern shows the hierarchy as divinely ordained and proper.
